claims.statement: GraphIndex and the LLM wiki have SEPARATE store contracts with separate backend implementations (GraphIndexPersistence/SQLitePersistence vs BaseWikiStore); no shared seam exists today, so 'the Postgres backend' must pick its contract explicitly.

hybrid_search already exists on PgVectorStore (dense+ColBERT, Python-side weighted merge, SQLAlchemy) — the brainstorm's 'no existe hybrid_search()' is false at the vector-store layer and true only for the graph/wiki store contracts.

No BM25 over Postgres exists to plug into: the only Postgres FTS artifact is a hardcoded-English GIN tsvector index. Real BM25 lives in bm25s (pageindex), SQLite FTS5 (wiki + graphindex), and VectorSeedPolicy. D6's FTS leg must be built new; the reusable assets are the RRF pattern and the reranker seam.

The re-ranking seam is exactly as the brainstorm assumed: AbstractReranker + factory + LocalCrossEncoderReranker (HuggingFace), with a proven consumption pattern in HybridPageIndexSearch._apply_reranker.

ground_claim(claim: str) -> GroundingResult grounds via stable edge-id paths over the in-memory graph; no chunk FK exists anywhere, so evidence_ref is a brand-new field with no existing consumer — OQ2 is a design decision, not archaeology.

The 'asyncpg, no SQLAlchemy' invariant holds for core modules (core/hooks/postgres.py, eval/sink.py, retrieval/pin.py) but NOT for the vector-store layer (PgVectorStore is SQLAlchemy). An asyncpg graphindex backend has precedent but cannot reuse PgVectorStore connection machinery — and D6's 'one roundtrip' claim depends on where embeddings live (U4).

OQ4 resolved: the wiki store suite IS backend-parametrized (params=['sqlite','memory'], Arango gated separately); the graphindex parity bar is the commit-protocol behavioral suite. A Postgres param slots in like Arango (live-DB gated).

A graphindex Postgres backend must also implement the graph commit protocol (apply_update/revert_commit with pre-images) to reach parity — recently landed on BOTH existing backends and used by GraphPublisher for agent memory. Postgres transactions make this strictly easier than Arango's lock-based serialization.

No temporal support (tstzrange/valid_from) exists in any backend, and no in-flight Postgres backend work exists — greenfield, no collision. Schema-v2 symbols (wiki) just landed and are still moving; a wiki-plane backend would need the symbol surface or graceful skip.

hypotheses.statement: Implement the Postgres backend as a THIRD GraphIndex persistence backend (persist_postgres.py, asyncpg, schema graphindex.*) mirroring the GraphIndexPersistence public API including the commit protocol, with the bitemporal schema (D1-D5) native to it; the one-pass hybrid (D6) is new work on this backend — its FTS leg is built (not reused), its RRF follows the pageindex pattern in SQL, its reranker leg reuses parrot/rerankers. A Postgres BaseWikiStore is a separate, optional follow-up feature. [AMENDED by Q&A: U1 chose BOTH contracts over one shared graphindex.* schema, so the feature also delivers a Postgres BaseWikiStore view of the same schema.]
hypotheses.reasoning: The brainstorm's temporal schema (concept_id/node_versions/edges) maps 1:1 to graphindex models, not wiki pages; the two contracts are separate today and merging them is a bigger architectural change than the brainstorm scopes.

unknowns.question: Which contract does the Postgres backend implement first: GraphIndexPersistence (persist_postgres.py), BaseWikiStore (PostgresWikiStore), or both over one graphindex.* schema? The codebase shows two separate seams (C1); the brainstorm's temporal schema maps naturally to graphindex.
options: a) GraphIndex persistence only (recommended by evidence)
b) Both from the start, one shared schema
unknowns.user_answer: Both contracts over ONE shared graphindex.* Postgres schema: the backend implements GraphIndexPersistence (incl. commit protocol) AND BaseWikiStore against the same schema. Bigger than hypothesis-1 scope; the spec must define how wiki pages map onto nodes/node_versions.

options: a) Core, next to persist.py/persist_sqlite.py (siblings live there)
unknowns.user_answer: Core package, next to the siblings: packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/knowledge/graphindex/ (persist_postgres.py; wiki-plane store file location settled in the spec). asyncpg gated as an optional extra.

unknowns.question: For the one-pass hybrid (D6): do embeddings move INTO the graphindex.* schema (pgvector column managed via asyncpg — true one roundtrip) or stay in PgVectorStore (SQLAlchemy — the graph/FTS legs and the KNN leg become two roundtrips fused in Python)?
options: b) Stay in PgVectorStore, fuse in Python (reuses existing ingestion)
c) Sprint 1-2 without KNN leg; decide with OQ3 spike
unknowns.user_answer: RESOLVED at review gate: PgVectorStore is NOT reused (it is SQLAlchemy); the graphindex-postgres backend is asyncpg — this is MANDATORY. Embeddings live in the graphindex.* schema managed via asyncpg (true one-pass). The re-ranking seam (parrot/rerankers) and the BM25/RRF machinery patterns ARE reused.

unknowns.question: Migration of existing Arango graphs (OQ6): export/import tool in scope, or fresh ingests only?
unknowns.user_answer: Fresh ingests only in v1; existing Arango tenants stay on Arango. No export/import tool in scope.
